title: Day 7 Knowledge Check: PEFT / LoRA Fine-Tuning

questions.question: How does LoRA reduce GPU memory and training cost compared to full fine-tuning?

options.A: It freezes base model weights and trains two small low-rank matrices (A and B) whose product approximates weight updates.
options.B: It deletes 98% of the transformer layers permanently.
options.C: It converts the LLM into a regex script.

questions.explanation: LoRA decomposes delta-W into A (d x r) and B (r x d), slashing trainable parameters by >98%.
questions.implication: Teams can fine-tune specialized domain adapters on modest single-GPU workstations instead of multi-node clusters.

questions.question: When should you choose LoRA fine-tuning over Qdrant RAG?

options.A: When teaching the SLM a strict output style, domain jargon, or tool-calling format—not for storing rapidly changing SOP facts.
options.B: Whenever a runbook IP address changes.

questions.explanation: Use RAG for dynamic facts ('what to know') and LoRA for consistent formatting/behavior ('how to act').
questions.implication: Baking volatile facts into model weights causes stale hallucinations and forces expensive retraining cycles.

questions.question: Why can a single base Qwen2.5-Coder model serve multiple domains with LoRA in production?

options.A: Lightweight adapter weights (~20MB) can be hot-swapped per tenant/domain on top of one shared base model in VRAM.
options.B: Because LoRA adapters require zero disk space.

questions.explanation: Multi-LoRA serving shares one base model across many specialized domain adapters.
questions.implication: Dramatically reduces GPU VRAM footprint when supporting multiple enterprise teams.
